query: What signals suggest an agent's tickets will take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: issue_type_or_category
per_column.rationale: Issue type is knowable at ticket creation and plausibly correlates with how long resolution takes; a legitimate predictor outside the focus variable.

per_column.name: assigned_agent_or_resolver
per_column.rationale: The assigned agent is known at/near intake and different agents/teams have different throughput; directly relevant to the query about agent-level signals. Legitimate predictor.

per_column.name: issue_scope_or_impact_scale
per_column.rationale: Scope/impact (system-wide vs single-user) is determinable early and plausibly drives resolution effort and duration. Valid predictor, not a function of resolution_time.

per_column.name: root_cause_mechanism_or_failure_pattern
per_column.rationale: Root cause is typically established during/after diagnosis, not reliably known before resolution. Using confirmed failure mechanism risks post-outcome leakage rather than a pre-outcome predictor.

per_column.name: is_recurring_or_duplicate_issue
per_column.rationale: Recurrence/duplication status can be assessed at intake and plausibly relates to resolution speed (known fixes vs novel problems). Legitimate predictor.

per_column.name: single_agent_ownership_or_no_reassignment
per_column.rationale: Whether a ticket had no reassignment is only fully known once the ticket is worked/closed; reassignment history unfolds over the ticket lifetime and correlates mechanically with duration. Leakage.

per_column.name: extended_time_to_final_closure_or_last_update_lag
per_column.rationale: This is essentially a thresholded version of the elapsed time to closure/last update -- a restatement/deterministic function of resolution_time itself. Direct leakage.

per_column.name: infrastructure_dependency
per_column.rationale: The dependent infrastructure is known at intake and plausibly affects resolution time, though it largely duplicates issue_type_or_category. Still a valid (if redundant) predictor.

judge.rationale: Five columns (issue type, assigned agent, scope/impact, recurrence, infrastructure dependency) are legitimate pre-outcome predictors, and the agent field is especially on-point for the query. However issue_type_or_category and infrastructure_dependency are near-duplicates, reducing independent leverage. Three columns are problematic: extended_time_to_final_closure is a direct restatement of resolution_time, single_agent_ownership/no_reassignment depends on lifecycle history that unfolds with duration, and root_cause_mechanism is generally established only during resolution -- all leakage. The valid set gives moderate genuine leverage but is diluted by redundancy and contaminated by clear leakage columns.
